subtype: Approach: side income to cover essential costs [Revision]
passage: Nandini asked, "Avni, what did you do when a month passed with no offers?" Well, I didn't panic first. I looked at rent. It was due in ten days and my savings weren't going to stretch. Then I looked at what I could do fast. I took two online tutoring students in maths, and started writing short pieces for a small magazine. It wasn't much, but it covered the rent. The important part was this: I could keep applying without taking any job just to stop the fear. A friend had jumped at a bad offer and regretted it. I adjusted my plan instead of dropping it. Paying the rent gave me space to be choosy, and that was worth more than the money itself.

qa.q: How many online tutoring students did Avni take?
qa.a: Avni took two online tutoring students in maths.

qa.q: What did Avni feel about taking on side work?
qa.a: Avni felt relief at covering the rent and at not having to grab a bad job to stop the fear.

qa.q: What could Avni do if the side income drops, and why?
qa.a: Avni could spread the search wider and ask more people for tutoring leads, because a second income source keeps pressure off.

qa.q: How might the friend who jumped at a bad offer see Avni's choice?
qa.a: The friend may feel a twinge of regret and envy, since Avni had space to be choosy.

grounding: After a month without offers, a person takes online tutoring and freelance writing to cover rent while searching, avoiding a poor hasty offer.

subtype: Approach: side income to cover essential costs [Revision]
passage:
I'm Suraj, and Simran and I share a flat in Indore. After her layoff she spent the first month doing nothing but applying, twelve hours a day, and getting nothing back. By the end of it she was checking her bank balance every hour and talking about taking a call-centre job she'd have hated.
Then one evening she turned her laptop toward me and said, 'Rent is ₹9,000. I need that covered so I can stop panicking.' She'd found two things: tutoring maths online to school students in the evenings, and writing short product articles for a small website. Neither was much. Together, she thought, around ₹10,000.
She took both. Mornings for applications, evenings for tutoring, weekends for writing. I noticed she stopped checking the balance so often.
In the seventh week she turned down the call-centre offer. Two weeks later she got an analyst interview. I don't know how she felt inside, but she looked like she could breathe.

qa.q: What does Simran checking her balance every hour suggest?
qa.a: She was anxious and close to panic, which was pushing her toward a job she would have hated.

qa.q: Which change helped Simran most, and why?
qa.a: Covering the rent with tutoring and writing; it eased the pressure so she could refuse a poor offer and keep searching.

qa.q: How does the change look to Suraj?
qa.a: Suraj notices the balance-checking stop and sees her able to breathe, while admitting not knowing her inner feelings.

grounding: Shows a job-seeker taking online tutoring and freelance writing after a month without offers, covering rent and avoiding a poor hasty offer.

subtype: Approach: side income to cover essential costs [Revision]
passage:
Week 4, Monday. Raghav has sent thirty applications and has ₹6,000 left. Rent of ₹8,000 is due on the 1st. He tells Shankar on the phone he might take the first job that calls, anything. Shankar asks, 'What can you do from home this week?'
Week 5, Thursday. Raghav has two things running. He tutors English online to three school students, an hour each evening. He writes short blog posts for a small travel company, paid per piece. His laptop screen has two windows: job portals on the left, a tutoring timetable on the right. The first payments cover half the rent.
Week 8, Saturday. The rent is paid. When a sales role with a two-year bond calls, he asks for the terms and says no. He is still searching, but not with his heart racing any more.

qa.q: How much rent was due on the 1st?
How is Raghav feeling by week 8 compared with week 4?
qa.a: Calmer and less desperate, no longer ready to take anything, because the rent is covered.

qa.q: What else could Raghav do to keep side work from swallowing the search?
qa.a: Fix set hours for tutoring and writing, as the two windows suggest, and check each week that applications still get enough time.

qa.q: How does Shankar's question change things for Raghav?
qa.a: Shankar steers Raghav from panic to a practical step, which leads to the tutoring and writing work.

grounding: Shows a job-seeker adding online tutoring and freelance writing after a month without offers, covering rent and turning down a poor offer.
